paper_title: Randomness Efficient Testing of Sparse Black Box Identities of Unbounded Degree over the Reals
statement: Note that our algorithm also allows for a so-called time-randomness tradeoff like some of 1 the previous tests mentioned in the introduction do. When  > mn , then we just run the 1 algorithm with some constant error probability and decrease the error probability to mn by doing a random walk on an expander with an additional O(log mn) random bits. When 1  ≤ mn then increase the success probability by just spending more time instead of more random bits by just running over all choices for the extra O(log2 1 ) random bits and doing a majority vote. The running time in the second case is only quasipolynomial in 1 , however. It remains an open problem whether we can bring down the number of random bits to O(log m), which would match the lower bound of (1 − ) · log m. One approach could be to decrease the number of random bits used in the Schwartz-Zippel Hitting Set Generator. While it is clear that we do an overapproximation on the number of monomials for many polynomials in the proof, it is not clear how we can use this fact.
